s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal mass with obstructive jaundice and hemobilia
salient_findings: Progressive enlargement of the right-lobe mass
Obstruction of the right hepatic bile duct
key_facts: History of partial resection of a presumed benign hepatic lesion
Multiple sessions of transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) for hemobilia
Six episodes of hemobilia treated with TAE
Alpha-fetoprotein and PIVKA-II within normal limits
Liver edge palpable four fingerbreadths below the xiphoid process
10 × 15 cm multilocular oval mass with papillary infoldings in the right hepatic lobe on abdominal ultrasonography

raw.champion: Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct
raw.rationale: Papillary adenocarcinoma in situ or papillary adenoma with severe atypia found in biliary cytology, and obstruction of the right hepatic bile duct with dilation of peripheral bile ducts

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: While cholangiocarcinoma is a possible diagnosis, the presence of papillary adenocarcinoma in situ and specific bile duct obstruction patterns suggest a more specific subtype like intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct

rejected.label: Mucinous cystic neoplasm of the liver
rejected.why: Although mucinous cystic neoplasm is a consideration due to the cystic nature of the lesion, the presence of papillary adenocarcinoma in situ and the specific location and nature of the bile duct obstruction point towards an intraductal process

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: This option is less likely due to the specific findings of papillary adenocarcinoma in situ and the pattern of bile duct involvement, which are more characteristic of intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct

rejected.label: Papillary cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary cholangiocarcinoma could be considered due to the papillary features, but the detailed description of the intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct fits better with the combination of clinical, imaging, and cytological findings
